text:
mia: FYI customer 'paprtrail' reporting intermittent API timeouts and 502/503s starting ~02:10 UTC. They gave request_id r-9f3a and a sample curl. Impacting a few endpoints, high tail latency.

raj: Can you paste the sample curl + request_id and any runner logs you have? Also which model/version are they hitting?

mia: Sample repro (from customer):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-rw-13b-infer-v2","input":"<very long context>...","stream":false}'
```
request_id: r-9f3a
Attached snippet from runner logs around crash: 
```
[02:11:07] infer-runner[pid:3245]: Allocating KV cache 8.2GB
[02:11:08] infer-runner[pid:3245]: CUDA error: out of memory
[02:11:09] infer-runner[pid:3245]: Segmentation fault (core dumped)
[02:11:09] containerd: killing container infer-runner-3245: exit code 139
[02:11:10] k8s: pod restart backoff
```

alex: That log looks like a GPU OOM followed by a segfault and container restart. Do we know the typical context length? Also whether KV prefetch is enabled for that customer route?

mia: Customer says they sometimes send ~18k-25k tokens. Batch size reported = 1 but they do long single requests. KV prefetch = enabled on their dedicated route.

raj: Immediate mitigations: 1) Route this customer's traffic to the smaller quantized variant (gpt-rw-13b-q4) as a fallback for 30m. 2) Disable KV prefetch for their route to avoid big allocations. 3) Add an autoscale burst to give them headroom. I'll trigger routing change now.

deploy-bot: routing-change: Applied fallback for route paprtrail -> gpt-rw-13b-q4 (rollout: 100% fallback) by raj at 02:18 UTC :white_check_mark:

alex: Good. Also please grab full core + backtrace from the node that crashed and nvml info. Commands we need: 
```bash
# on node with crash
sudo gcore -o /tmp/core.infer 3245 || true
sudo gdb -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt full' -ex quit /usr/bin/infer-runner /tmp/core.infer > /tmp/backtrace.txt
# nvml memory snapshot
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY > /tmp/nvmem.txt
# collect dmesg around crash
dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-crash.txt
```
Please upload tar to incident storage and paste link.

mia: Collected and uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-archive/3770001111/paprtrail.tar.gz (backtrace + nvmem + dmesg). Upload verified.

alex: From initial backtrace it looks like allocator hit a boundary during prefetch and then a segfault in the attention kernel. We'll triage deeper in runtime/eng-ml. For now fallback + disable prefetch should stop immediate restarts.

cs-ops: Notified customer, explained mitigation and offered a one-week credit. Customer accepted the temporary fallback, reported immediate improvement in latency.

raj: Filed INF-4823 and assigned to eng-runtime (alex) and eng-ml (sara) for root-cause and a patch to guard against large prefetch allocations. Monitoring for 2 hours; will re-evaluate for permanent fix.

mia: Marking this thread mitigated. Will update if regressions. :thumbsup:
